# Open-license 3D models

Ready-made **CC0** (public domain) models from [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com) that complement the
Meshy-generated props (see [meshy.md](meshy.md)). No attribution is required for CC0; authors are credited anyway.
Machine-readable manifest: `src/data/generated/open-models.json` (separate from `models.json`).

Rebuild / extend: `node scripts/assets/fetch-open-models.mjs` (`--force`, `--only=id,…`, `--cache=dir`, `--check`).
Sources are the Poly Haven 1k glTF downloads (md5-verified against the API) plus, for foliage, the 1k alpha map.

## Conventions

- Files: `public/assets/models/open/<id>.glb` — meshopt-compressed geometry (`EXT_meshopt_compression`,
  `KHR_mesh_quantization`; drei `useGLTF` decodes it by default), WebP textures ≤ 1024 px.
- Units metres, Y up, real-world size (except `rock-limestone-slab`, scaled ×10). Pivot at the bottom centre,
  except the ground-patch scans `rock-coast-ledge`, `beach-pebble-patch` and `stone-fire-pit`, whose pivot is the
  scan's own ground plane (they dip below y = 0; see `pivot` in the manifest). Transforms baked. "Forward" is the
  source's front view (+Z); most of these are rotation-agnostic.
- Materials: base colour + OpenGL normal map + Poly Haven ARM map bound as metallicRoughness **and** occlusion
  (R = AO, G = roughness, B = metal). Poly Haven marks every material double-sided; for closed opaque props
  (rocks, vessels) `side = FrontSide` is safe and cheaper. Normal maps need runtime tangents (three.js derives them).
- Foliage: the source alpha map is merged into the base colour, `alphaMode: MASK` (cutoff 0.5), double-sided.
  Prefer `alphaToCoverage` with MSAA, or keep `alphaTest`; avoid transparent sorting.
- **Variant sets** (`variants` in the manifest): each variant is its own top-level node named `<id>_<suffix>`,
  pivoted at its own bottom centre, so all variants **overlap at the origin**. Pick one with
  `gltf.scene.getObjectByName(name)` (clone or use its geometry for `InstancedMesh`); do not add the whole scene.

### Integration notes

- `rock-coast-ledge` — Scan includes its own ground skirt (sand/pebbles). Pivot is the scan's ground plane: place y=0 on the beach surface (the skirt dips to -0.25 m). Real size, ~4 m across.
- `rock-boulder-block` — Real size ~2.4 x 1.5 x 3.1 m. Scale 0.5-1.5 and rotate freely for variety.
- `rock-boulder-pale` — Real size ~1.4 x 0.5 x 0.75 m.
- `rock-rubble-cluster` — One mesh, ~2.5 x 0.9 x 1.2 m. Bottom is flat; sink slightly.
- `rock-boulder-jagged` — Real size ~1.3 x 1.0 x 1.8 m.
- `rock-limestone-slab` — Source is a 21 cm hand-sample scan (Poly Haven "Moon Rock 01"); scaled x10 to ~2.1 x 0.8 x 1.1 m. Texture is therefore softer up close; fine at >3 m.
- `stones-small` — Variant nodes stones-small_a..e, each pivoted at its own bottom centre (all overlap at the origin). Scale up to x3 for cobbles.
- `beach-pebble-patch` — Ground-patch scan ~4.6 x 3.9 m, rocks up to ~0.4 m high, irregular sandy rim. Pivot is the scan's ground plane: place y=0 on the beach surface.
- `helichrysum-clump` — Species is South African (Stinkkruid); visually close to Mediterranean helichrysum/santolina. 4 variants, 0.2-0.35 m wide; scale x1.5-2.5 for garden clumps. Alpha-tested leaves (MASK 0.5), double-sided.
- `calendula-wild` — Species is South African (Ursinia). 5 variants, 0.15-0.45 m wide. Alpha-tested, double-sided.
- `iceplant-coastal` — 8 variants, 5-30 cm. Alpha-tested, double-sided.
- `nettle-clump` — 6 variants, 6-22 cm tall; scale x2-4 for mature clumps. Alpha-tested, double-sided.
- `dry-scrub` — Species is South African (wild rooibos). 5 variants, 0.3-0.85 m. Twigs/leaves alpha-tested, trunk opaque.
- `yellow-wildflower` — Species is South African (Empodium). 5 variants, 0.1-0.27 m. Very cheap (~3k tris for all). Alpha-tested.
- `dandelion` — 5 variants, 0.12-0.22 m. Alpha-tested.
- `marble-bust` — Renaissance-style but reads as a Roman Republican/Julio-Claudian portrait. 0.27 x 0.51 x 0.30 m (life size). Face looks to +Z.
- `urn-planter` — The source houseplant (leaves/stem) is removed. 0.47 x 0.53 m. Gravel top sits ~0.45 m above the base.
- `terracotta-pot` — 0.27 x 0.22 m. Empty (no soil).
- `wooden-bowl` — 0.13 x 0.07 m.
- `pomegranate` — 11 cm. Decimated from 8k tris.
- `wooden-bucket` — 0.37 x 0.55 m including the raised handle.
- `wooden-tub` — 0.62 x 0.35 m.
- `folding-stool` — 0.53 x 0.44 x 0.55 m. Slatted wooden seat (a Roman one would have leather) — fine at a glance.
- `wicker-basket` — 0.38 x 0.12 x 0.30 m. Decimated from 22k tris; the weave lives mostly in the normal map.
- `jetty-section` — One module (section_02) of Poly Haven "Modular Wooden Pier": 2.5 m wide, deck 2.9 m long along Z, one pair of piles. Pile feet at y=0, deck top at 3.61 m, pile tops 3.84 m: sink it so the deck is ~1 m above the water. Chain copies every 2.91 m along Z and close the open end with rocks or a second module.
- `driftwood` — 3 variants, 0.8-1.3 m long.
- `stone-fire-pit` — 1.45 m across. Pivot is the ground plane (the ash bowl dips ~0.19 m below it). Add a small flame/smoke effect at the centre if lit.

## Gaps (not found as open models)

Nothing suitable (CC0/CC-BY, direct download, matching style) was found for: roses, lilies, irises, lavender,
rosemary, poppies, wild fennel, ivy, acanthus, vines; a 1st-century boat; Roman-style statues, pedestals and
garden urns/kraters (beyond the bust and the urn planter); amphorae, jugs, oil lamps; ropes and fishing nets;
stone well-head, sundial, column fragments, pergola beams. These are left to Meshy or procedural geometry.
